# Ryu shortest binary32 formatting: known answers, from upstream's own suite.
#
# Provenance
#   Every expected string below is the literal upstream asserts, copied from
#   the gtest cases of `ASSERT_F2S(...)` in ryu/ryu/tests/f2s_test.cc at the
#   pinned upstream revision 4c0618b0e44f7ef027ebae05d2cc7812048f7c8f.
#   Nothing in this file was computed by this fork.
#
# One upstream case is guarded by `#ifndef _WIN32` (f2s_test.cc, Regression):
# upstream records that MSVC's *compiler* rounds the literal 7.038531E-26f to
# the next float up, and expects the other answer on every other compiler.
# That is a property of the C front end that parses the literal, not of the
# machine that runs the test, and Zig parses float literals with its own
# correctly rounded parser on every target, so the `#ifndef _WIN32` arm is
# the answer here for all six.  The `_WIN32` arm is not copied.
#
# Line format
#   <input-spec> TAB <expected string>
#
#   input-spec is one of
#     zero | negzero | nan | inf | neginf
#         the five non-finite/signed cases of the f2s_test.cc Basic case
#     bits   <8 hex digits>
#         upstream's int32Bits2Float(0x...) helper
#     lit    <decimal literal>
#         the upstream C literal, with the `f` suffix dropped
#
#   Blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored.
#
# The exponent marker is upstream's: uppercase `E`, no `+`, no zero padding
# (`1E0`, `1E-45`, `3.4028235E38`).  That spelling is part of the known
# answer and is not normalised anywhere.
zero	0E0
negzero	-0E0
lit 1.0	1E0
lit -1.0	-1E0
nan	NaN
inf	Infinity
neginf	-Infinity
